summary: The root غلي primarily means to boil or bubble up, like water or a pot.

headwords.def: غَلَتِ القِدْرُ , aor. تَغْلِى , inf. n. غَلْىٌ and غَلَيَانٌ , (S, MA, Msb, K,) The cooking-pot boiled; (MA, &c.;) and غَلِيَت , aor. تَغْلَى , is an unusual dial. var. thereof, the former being the more chaste; (Msb;) or غَلِيَت is not allowable. (S.) [Hence غَلَى said of a liquor, It estuated: it effervesced: it fermented: see نَبِيذٌ And hence] يَغْلِى دَمُهُ [as though meaning (assumed tropical:) His blood is fit to be shed ] is a phrase like رَابَ دَمُهُ , [q. v.], said of one who has exposed himself to slaughter: his blood being likened to milk that has become thick, and fit to be churned. (A in art. روب .) And غَلِىَ الرَّجُلُ , like رَضِىَ in measure [but see what has been said of this form of the verb above], (tropical:)

headwords.gloss: He rubbed the man over; perfumed him, with; He daubed

parts.t: saluting from afar, and making a sign.

headwords.def: غَلَّىَ see 4, in two places. غلّى الرَّجُلَ , inf. n. تَغْلِيَةٌ , He rubbed the man over, or perfumed him, with غَالِيَة . (TA.) And غلّى لِحْيَتَهُ (Mgh, O,) Msb, all in art. غلف ) بِالغَالِيَةِ (O, ibid.) He daubed, or smeared, his beard with غَالِيَة ; as also غَلَّلَهَا . (Mgh, O, Msb, ibid. [See 1 in art. غلف .]) And تَغْلِيَةٌ signifies also The saluting from afar, and making a sign. (K.)

headwords.gloss: He made the cooking-pot to boil; Pour thou out water, and make it to boil; I made the olive-oil and the like to boil

parts.t: He made the cooking-pot to boil.
(S, * MA, K. *) IDrd mentions, among some of the sayings of the people of former ages,
Pour thou out water, and make it to boil
I made the olive-oil and the like to boil

headwords.def: اغلى القِدْرَ , (S, MA, K,) and , (K,) He made the cooking-pot to boil. (S, * MA, K. *) IDrd mentions, among some of the sayings of the people of former ages, أُنَّ مَآءً [ Pour thou out water, and make it to boil ]. (TA.) And one says, أَغْلَيْتُ الزَّيْتَ وَنَحْوَهُ [ I made the olive-oil and the like to boil ], inf. n. إِغْلَآءٌ . (Msb.)

تغلّى (S, Msb, K) بِالغَالِيَةِ (S, Msb) He (a man, S, Msb) perfumed himself, (S, * Msb, K,) or rubbed himself over, (K,) with غَالِيَة ; (S, Msb, K;) and signifies the same; (IDrd, O in art. غلف ;) as also تَغَلَّلَ , (Msb, and O in art. غلف ,) and اِغْتَلَّ . (O in that art.)

headwords.gloss: A vessel of copper; brass; in which water is heated; thus called by the people of Syria; the same that is called

parts.t: in which water is heated; thus called by the people of Syria; the same that is called

headwords.def: غَلَّايَةٌ A vessel of copper [or brass ], in which water is heated; thus called by the people of Syria; the same that is called مِحَمٌّ [q. v.] and قُمْقُمٌ and قُمْقُمَةٌ . (Msb voce قُمْقُمٌ .)

headwords.def: غَالِيَةٌ [ Galia moschata, ] a sort of perfume, (S, K,) well known; (K;) a certain compound of perfumes; (Msb;) musk mixed or boiled [ with other perfumes ]; (MA;) or a perfume composed of musk and ambergris and camphor and oil of ben: (KL:) it is said that the first who called it thus was Suleymán Ibn-'Abd-El-Melik; (S, TA;) and he did so because it is a compound boiled together upon the fire: or it was thus named by Mo'áwiyeh; the case being, that 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Jaafar went in to him, and the odour of perfume was diffusing itself from him; so he said, “ What is thy perfume, O 'Abd-Allah? ” and he answered, “ musk and ambergris combined with oil of ben; ” whereupon Mo'áwiyeh said, غَالِيَةٌ , meaning highpriced:
